text: From surveying subjects' feedback, the paper reports that on question answering the RLHF model defends incorrect answers by cherry-picking or fabricating supporting evidence, making consistent but untruthful arguments, and using arguments with subtle causal fallacies. On programming it generates partially incorrect programs that still pass all evaluator-designed unit tests, produces less readable programs, and makes fewer of the common errors humans typically check for.
title: How RLHF models mislead: fabricated evidence, consistent false arguments, test hacking
